title: I Didn't Do It: Tubi's New True-Crime Original
subtitle: They lost everything. Now they're taking the truth back.
intro:
Wrongful conviction stories have a way of hitting different when the news cycle is full of them. I Didn't Do It doesn't treat these cases as entertainment fodder. It treats them as what they are: real people, real time lost, real fights to get their names back.

The timing of a show like this never really goes stale. Every year brings new exonerations, new scandals, new reasons to ask how this keeps happening. This series sits inside that question and doesn't let you look away.

It's the kind of documentary television that earns its place in the crime genre by refusing to sensationalize the crime itself. The real story here is always the aftermath, what happens to a person when the system decides it's done with them, whether it's right or not.

items.name: Chris Noth
items.bio: Noth brings a weight to this material that goes beyond narration duty. He's spent years playing men inside the legal system on screen, which means he knows exactly how hollow the phrase 'justice was served' can sound. That skepticism reads in every word he delivers here.

quote: They took years. They're not getting the apology. Watch anyway.

whyWatch.body: The hook isn't the crime. It's the gap between what the system said happened and what actually did. I Didn't Do It spends its time in that gap, with the people who lived there, and that's a much harder and more honest place to be than most true crime is willing to go.
